npcs.history: Dwight Spann has run a Sturdivant Land and Timber crew in the pine upriver for eighteen years, since Harlan Voss hired him. He lives alone in a trailer at Riverbend and goes up to Sturdivant House every morning for his orders.

npcs.name: Burl Satterfield
npcs.role: June's husband, who fixes outboard motors
npcs.look: Wide, red-faced man of sixty-six in bib overalls, with a lineman's scarred hands and a bent outboard propeller he files smooth while he talks.
npcs.voice: Talks too loud after forty years around power lines, says what's that? and then answers what he thought you said.
npcs.goal: Keep June from wearing herself out on everybody at Riverbend.
npcs.secret: He rebuilt the motors on two of Wade Purvis's johnboats this fall for cash and told June the money came from his pension.
npcs.history: Burl Satterfield climbed power poles for the co-op for forty years and retired in 2019 with a pension and bad hearing. He and June moved to Riverbend that year, and he fixes outboard motors for anyone at the landing who brings him one. Wiley Tackett was his best friend.

npcs.name: Amber Lott
npcs.role: Tammy's daughter, who died at nineteen
npcs.look: Remembered as a freckled girl of nineteen with a pink streak dyed in her hair, a nose ring and a laugh you could hear from the far end of the Riverbend loop.
npcs.voice: Talked fast and loud and called everybody by a nickname she had made up for them, and her mother still uses a few of them without meaning to.
npcs.goal: Wanted to finish a nursing assistant course in Clayburn and get herself and her brother out of Riverbend.
npcs.secret: She had been clean for two months when she died, and the pills that killed her were the first she had bought since telling June Satterfield she was done with them.
npcs.history: Amber grew up in the Lott Trailer and worked a drive-through window in Clayburn after she quit school. She died at Riverbend in August, at nineteen, and is buried in Riverside Cemetery under a funeral-home marker until there is money for a stone.

npcs.name: Ruth Haskins
npcs.role: Lamar's late wife and Virgil's daughter
npcs.look: Remembered as a tall, sunburned woman of forty-seven in a seed company cap, who drove the grain truck herself at harvest.
npcs.voice: Laughed at her own jokes before she got to the end of them, and said well, bless it whenever anything broke on the farm.
npcs.goal: Wanted to see the farm paid off and Trent settled before she was fifty.
npcs.secret: The year before she died she told her father the farm was two seasons from losing its equipment, and made him promise never to let Lamar sell out to the Sturdivants.
npcs.history: Ruth was Virgil Odom's only daughter and married Lamar Haskins at twenty-two. She kept the farm's books, drove the grain truck at harvest and taught Sunday school at Riverside Baptist until the cancer. She died three winters ago, and her father moved out to the farm the spring after.

npcs.name: Amos Sturdivant
npcs.role: Vada's father, who fought the state for the bridge in 1938
npcs.look: Known from one photograph in Town Hall: a lean man in a white suit at the bridge ribbon-cutting in 1938, hat in hand and squinting at the camera.
npcs.voice: Said to have talked like a preacher and bargained like a horse trader, and never to have written down a promise he could make out loud.
npcs.goal: Wanted a bridge at Lockett's Ferry with the Sturdivant name on the plaque, and got both.
npcs.secret: He ran whiskey into the dry county from the 1920s into the 1950s, the last years with Elbert Gentry rowing it, and the cash he paid the state highway department in 1938 is why the bridge was built here and not somewhere else.
npcs.history: Amos Sturdivant bought the bottomland and the hill in the 1920s and built Sturdivant House. He spent three years fighting the state for a bridge and stood on it the day it opened in 1938. His name is on the plaque at the town end of the old bridge.

npcs.name: Harlan Voss
npcs.died: October 2014, a heart attack in the timber woods
npcs.role: Vada's late husband and Carter's father, who ran the timber side of the business
npcs.look: Remembered as a heavy, red-faced man of seventy-one in khaki work clothes and a straw hat, with a tally book in his shirt pocket and mud to the knees.
npcs.voice: Talked timber prices to anyone who would listen, called every man buddy, and could not tell a story without starting it in the woods.
npcs.goal: Wanted Sturdivant Land and Timber to outlast him with Carter at the head of it.
npcs.secret: In his last years he borrowed against the timber from Garland Teasley without telling Vada, and the loans Carter is behind on now are his.
npcs.history: Harlan Voss came from upriver to buy timber, married Vada Sturdivant in 1977 and ran the timber side of the business for thirty years. Vada kept her name, and their son carries it. He died in the timber woods in 2014 and is buried beside her father.

npcs.name: Inez Crocker
npcs.role: Mavis's late mother, whose house the Mangums live in
npcs.look: Remembered as a small, sharp woman of sixty-nine in a quilted housecoat, with a church fan in one hand and the TV remote in the other.
npcs.voice: Told everybody exactly what she thought of them, to their face, and called it being honest.
npcs.goal: Wanted to die in her own house, owing nobody, with Mavis there.
npcs.secret: She signed a contract for deed with Sturdivant Land and Timber on the house in 2016 to pay her hospital bills, and Mavis never knew until the papers came after the funeral.
npcs.history: Inez Crocker lived in the white frame house up the river road for forty years and worked in the office at the paper mill until it closed. Mavis and Dewayne moved in to look after her in 2021. She died in that house in February of last year.

npcs.name: Asa Gentry
npcs.role: Elbert's granddaddy, who ran the last ferry
npcs.look: Known from the photographs in the Gentry House: a bent, white-bearded man in a slouch hat, standing at the ferry's sweep with the river high behind him.
npcs.voice: Said to have answered every question with the river's height that morning, and to have charged strangers double and widows nothing.
npcs.goal: Wanted the ferry to last as long as he did, and it nearly did.
npcs.secret: He took Amos Sturdivant's money to stop fighting the bridge in 1937, and the Gentrys have called it a fair price ever since.
npcs.history: Asa Gentry ran the Gentry ferry across the Lusk for fifty years, until the bridge opened in 1938 and the ferry was cut loose. He built the Gentry House, sat on its porch watching the bridge traffic for thirteen more years and died in the winter of 1951.

npcs.name: Wiley Tackett
npcs.role: the mechanic who ran the garage on Front Street for forty-five years
npcs.look: Remembered as a short, bowlegged man of seventy-seven in a work shirt with his name over the pocket, never without a cigarette.
npcs.voice: Talked to engines like they were mules, cussed them the same, and taught half the boys in town to change their own oil.
npcs.goal: Wanted Dewayne Mangum to have the garage when he was gone.
npcs.secret: He told Burl Satterfield he had left the garage to Dewayne, but the Sturdivants held the note on the building, and the will he left gave it back to them.
npcs.history: Wiley Tackett fixed cars in the garage on Front Street from 1979 until he got too sick to stand. Dewayne Mangum learned the trade under him before he went to work for Royce Pittman. The bay doors have been chained since he died, three springs ago.

npcs.name: Clyde Pittman
npcs.died: summer of 2009, a heart attack at the pumps
npcs.role: Royce's late daddy, who opened Pittman's in 1966
npcs.look: Remembered as a big, bald man of sixty-nine in a white station shirt, with a cigar he never lit and a ring of keys on his belt.
npcs.voice: Told the same six stories at the register for forty years, and Royce tells them now, word for word, as if they happened to him.
npcs.goal: Wanted the station to stay a Pittman's for as long as the highway ran past it.
npcs.secret: He borrowed against the station from Harlan Voss in 1998 to get through a bad year, and that note, rolled over and over, is the one Carter Sturdivant holds on Royce now.
npcs.history: Clyde Pittman built the station in 1966, when the highway still brought the trucks through town, and ran it until the day he died at the pumps in 2009. His photo still hangs over the register.

npcs.name: Dale Purvis
npcs.where: the state penitentiary, eight years into a fifteen-year sentence
npcs.reach: letters, and a collect call on Sunday nights; visiting is the second and fourth Saturday
npcs.role: Wade's younger brother and Colt's father, in the state penitentiary
npcs.look: Lean, gray-stubbled man of forty-nine in prison whites, with his brother's face gone harder and a cross tattooed on the back of each hand.
npcs.voice: Talks fast on the phone because the call is timed, asks about the river before he asks about anyone, and never says goodbye, only later.
npcs.goal: Make parole in two years and come home to the job on the river his brother has promised him.
npcs.secret: He took the whole charge that sent him away, a trailer load of stolen outboard motors, so that Wade would not go down with him, and his letters have started asking what that bought him.
npcs.history: Dale ran the river with Wade from the time they were boys. He was sentenced in 2018 over a trailer load of stolen outboard motors and has done eight years of fifteen at the state penitentiary. Colt was fourteen when he went in.

npcs.name: Warren Pettit
npcs.where: Calder, at his engineering firm on the courthouse square
npcs.reach: by email to his firm; he has stopped taking calls about the bridge
npcs.role: the consulting engineer from Calder who wrote the report that condemned the old bridge
npcs.look: Soft, pale man of fifty-one in a pressed polo shirt with his firm's logo on it, rimless glasses and a hard hat that has never been dirty.
npcs.voice: Talks in percentages and section numbers, says per the report instead of yes, and ends every call by saying he has another one.
npcs.goal: Get through the council meeting without being asked a question under oath, and get paid for the downstream design work.
npcs.secret: He wrote most of the bridge report from Virgil Odom's answers on the phone and the state's old files, and spent inspection day at lunch with Carter Sturdivant instead of under the spans.
npcs.history: Warren Pettit runs a two-man engineering firm in Calder that does bridge and culvert work for the state. He inspected the old bridge in April, and his report rated it critical. He has not been back to Lockett's Ferry since.

npcs.name: Renee Byrd
npcs.where: Calder, where she cleans teeth at a dental office near the hospital
npcs.reach: her number is in Hollis's phone, and she lets it ring
npcs.role: Hollis's daughter, a dental hygienist in Calder
npcs.look: Tidy, dark-haired woman of thirty-eight in navy scrubs, with her father's heavy eyebrows and a ring she turns when she is nervous.
npcs.voice: Polite and final; says I'm not doing this with you today, and means it.
npcs.goal: Keep her own family clear of her father's business.
npcs.secret: She knows what goes through Hollis's books because she kept them for him at sixteen, and that is the reason she stopped speaking to him.
npcs.history: Renee grew up in the apartment over the pawn shop and left for Calder at eighteen. She stopped speaking to her father in 2023, and when she married Scott Lindell in October 2024 she did not invite him.

npcs.name: Scott Lindell
npcs.where: Calder, where he runs the pharmacy counter at a drugstore by the interstate
npcs.reach: the pharmacy phone, or through Renee
npcs.role: Renee's husband, a pharmacist in Calder
npcs.look: Lanky, balding man of forty in a white pharmacy coat, with a lanyard of keys, rimless reading glasses and the careful smile of a man who counts pills.
npcs.voice: Mild and exact; repeats your question back before he answers it, and says let me check on that when he means no.
npcs.goal: Keep Renee happy and her father out of their life.
npcs.secret: He has met Hollis Byrd once, without Renee knowing: Hollis came to the pharmacy in the spring to ask about her, and Scott told him to go home.
npcs.history: Scott Lindell grew up in Calder and has run a pharmacy counter there for twelve years. He married Renee Byrd in October 2024 at a courthouse wedding with twenty guests and none of her family.

npcs.name: Celeste Bell
npcs.where: Calder, where she works nights in the emergency room at Calder Regional
npcs.reach: she calls her brother on Sunday nights, after her shift
npcs.role: Marcus Bell's sister, a nurse at Calder Regional
npcs.look: Tall, broad-shouldered woman of forty-six in green scrubs and running shoes, with short gray curls and her brother's heavy jaw.
npcs.voice: Tired and teasing; calls her brother Chief as if it were a private joke, and asks whether he is eating.
npcs.goal: Get her brother to quit before the job kills him, and come live near her in Calder.
npcs.secret: She has a spare room ready and a hospital security job lined up for Marcus, and she has not told him because she knows he would say no.
npcs.history: Celeste and Marcus are all that is left of the Bell family. She has worked nights in the emergency room at Calder Regional for twenty years and drives down to see him at Christmas.

npcs.name: Leah Dees
npcs.where: the Willows, a treatment program in Calder, since July
npcs.reach: one phone call a week on Thursday nights, and family visits on Sunday afternoons
npcs.role: Ray and Nadine's daughter and Micah's mother, in a treatment program in Calder
npcs.look: Thin, freckled woman of thirty-eight in a borrowed sweatshirt, with her mother's curls cut short and a plastic program bracelet on her wrist.
npcs.voice: Quiet and careful on the phone; says I'm doing the work when anyone asks how she is, and asks about Micah first.
npcs.goal: Finish the program this time and come home to Micah clean.
npcs.secret: She knows the program costs more each month than her parents have, she has guessed where Micah's money comes from, and she has said nothing.
npcs.history: Leah grew up in the Parsonage and had Micah at twenty-one. She has been in and out of treatment since he was small, and went into the Willows in Calder in July. Micah has lived with her parents since.

npcs.name: Stanley Wexler
npcs.where: Calder, where he owns two car washes and a laundromat besides the motor court
npcs.reach: by email; he answers within a day and never by phone
npcs.role: owner of the Riverview Motor Court, who runs it by email from Calder
npcs.look: Pink, heavyset man of sixty-three in a golf visor and a pastel shirt, known in town from one visit two years ago and the photo on his emails.
npcs.voice: Writes in capital letters and short lines, signs every email with his first name, and asks about the occupancy rate before anything else.
npcs.goal: Sell the motor court for what he paid for it before the bridge question drags its price down.
npcs.secret: He already has an offer on the motor court from Carter Sturdivant, good only if the council votes for the downstream site, and he has not told Mavis.
npcs.history: Stanley Wexler bought the Riverview Motor Court in 2019 as an investment and has been on the lot once since. He runs it through Mavis Mangum by email and wants the nightly counts by six every morning.

npcs.name: Calvin Ogletree
npcs.where: the county home in Clayburn, since the winter of 2021
npcs.reach: visiting hours every afternoon; he cannot use a phone
npcs.role: a former river hand who has been in the county home since a beating
npcs.look: Thin man of forty-four in a wheelchair by the window, with a dent in his skull under hair that grew back white.
npcs.voice: Speaks a word or two at a time, smiles at whoever comes in, and calls every visitor by his sister's name.
npcs.goal: Wants to go home, and asks his sister every visit when they are going.
npcs.secret: Before the beating he had started running cartons across the river on his own at night, under the Night Run's prices.
npcs.history: Calvin decked on towboats up and down the river in his twenties and came home to work the river and the timber. He was found beaten nearly to death below Purvis Landing one night in December 2021, and nobody was ever charged. He has lived at the county home since, and his sister visits every Sunday.

npcs.name: Bernice Ogletree
npcs.where: Clayburn, in a rented duplex four blocks from the county home
npcs.reach: she has a phone and answers it; she sees her brother every Sunday
npcs.role: Calvin's sister, who looks after him at the county home
npcs.look: Wiry, tired woman of fifty in a grocery store cashier's vest, with reading glasses pushed up on her head and her brother's photo on her phone.
npcs.voice: Flat and wary; asks who sent you before she answers anything, and says nobody from Lockett's Ferry ever came to see him.
npcs.goal: Find out who beat her brother and see them answer for it, and get her daughter Jodie home before the law finds her.
npcs.secret: A money order for two hundred dollars comes to her every month with no name on it, postmarked Lockett's Ferry, and she has kept every stub; her daughter Jodie, who skipped bail this summer, has written once from the same town under another name.
npcs.history: Bernice works the register at the grocery in Clayburn and has spent every Sunday afternoon at the county home since her brother was hurt. She has asked the sheriff about his case so often that the front desk knows her voice.

npcs.name: Hoyt Bramlett
npcs.where: Clayburn, at the sheriff's office in the courthouse basement
npcs.reach: the sheriff's office line; a deputy comes when called, in an hour or two
npcs.role: the county sheriff, at the courthouse in Clayburn
npcs.look: Barrel-chested man of sixty-one in a tan uniform and a gray felt cowboy hat, with a toothpick, a campaign pin and a belly over his belt buckle.
npcs.voice: Slow and friendly, like a man running for office, which he always is; calls everybody young man or young lady and promises to look into it.
npcs.goal: Win the contract to patrol Lockett's Ferry, with the money and the deputies that come with it, before the next election.
npcs.secret: He has wanted Marcus Bell's department gone for years, and he has told the mayor the county will patrol the town for half what the police cost, which it cannot.
npcs.history: Hoyt Bramlett has been sheriff since 2006 and runs eleven deputies across the county from the courthouse in Clayburn. He comes to Lockett's Ferry for funerals and elections, and his deputies and the town police do not get along.

npcs.name: Phillip Sayle
npcs.where: Calder, at a clinic for older patients near Calder Regional
npcs.reach: through his office, by appointment
npcs.role: a doctor in Calder who examines old people for the courts
npcs.look: Neat, silver-haired man of fifty-eight in a sport coat over a golf shirt, with a leather folder of forms and a soft voice made for bad news.
npcs.voice: Gentle and professional; uses your first name, asks what year it is as if it were small talk, and writes while you answer.
npcs.goal: Keep the guardianship work the lawyers in Calder send him.
npcs.secret: Neal Haverty has sent him eleven cases in five years, and he has found every one of the old people unfit.
npcs.history: Dr. Sayle runs a small practice for older patients in Calder and testifies in guardianship cases in three counties. People in Lockett's Ferry know him only by name.

npcs.name: Neal Haverty
npcs.where: Calder, in an office over the bank on the courthouse square
npcs.reach: his office phone; his paralegal returns calls
npcs.role: the Sturdivants' lawyer in Calder
npcs.look: Long-faced man of sixty in a gray suit, with half-glasses on a cord and a fountain pen he points like a finger.
npcs.voice: Dry and courteous; begins every sentence with as I understand it, and never says anything on the phone he would not say in court.
npcs.goal: Get the downstream right-of-way through before the state's money goes somewhere else, and bill Carter for every hour of it.
npcs.secret: He drew up Lamar Haskins's option papers knowing they are worthless while Vada is alive, and told Carter to keep the uncashed check as leverage.
npcs.history: Neal Haverty has handled Sturdivant business since Harlan Voss's day, from an office over the bank in Calder. He writes the letters people in Lockett's Ferry do not want to get.

npcs.name: Corinne Bolden
npcs.where: Clayburn, in the house she and Odessa grew up in, behind the courthouse
npcs.reach: Odessa drives over on her Sunday afternoons off; Corinne has a phone and a bad hip
npcs.role: Odessa's older sister, a retired school cook in Clayburn
npcs.look: Heavy, slow-moving woman of seventy in a church hat and orthopedic shoes, with a walker and her sister's same quiet way of watching.
npcs.voice: Talks about her hip, her pastor and her sister in that order, and calls Odessa baby girl though she is sixty-six.
npcs.goal: Keep the family house and be buried from it.
npcs.secret: She signed a contract for deed with Sturdivant Land and Timber to keep the house, and she has missed four payments that Odessa has quietly made for her.
npcs.history: Corinne cooked in the county school cafeteria in Clayburn for thirty-one years. She has lived alone in the family house behind the courthouse since 2020, and Odessa visits on her Sundays off.

npcs.name: Lynette Pruett
npcs.where: Clayburn, in the brick house she and Curtis bought in 2004
npcs.reach: she answers the phone when it is not Curtis
npcs.role: Curtis's wife, who put him out of their house in Clayburn
npcs.look: Petite, blonde woman of fifty in a bank teller's blazer, with a careful manicure and the patience of somebody who counts other people's money all day.
npcs.voice: Sweet as pie and twice as hard; says I'm sure you mean well, and hangs up.
npcs.goal: Keep the house and get Curtis to sign the divorce papers before the end of the year.
npcs.secret: She knows about the eleven hundred dollars Royce Pittman owes Curtis, and she has asked a lawyer whether it counts as marital property.
npcs.history: Lynette has been a teller at the bank in Clayburn for twenty-five years. She put Curtis out of their house last winter over his card games and his debts, and he has had a room at the Riverview Motor Court since.

npcs.name: Wendell Strunk
npcs.where: Clayburn, behind the counter of his title-loan office on the highway
npcs.reach: his office phone; he calls back the same day
npcs.role: owner of the title-loan outfit in Clayburn that Leon Varner collects for
npcs.look: Short, sun-spotted man of fifty-nine in a short-sleeved dress shirt and a clip-on tie, with a calculator watch and a gap in his front teeth.
npcs.voice: Cheerful about terrible news; says it's just business, buddy, and reads out an interest rate like a weather report.
npcs.goal: Turn every bad note in the county into a truck on his lot or a check in his drawer.
npcs.secret: He buys his bad debts from Garland Teasley through Leon Varner at a dime on the dollar, and he knows Teasley is selling because Teasley means to call in the Sturdivant loans soon.
npcs.history: Wendell Strunk opened his title-loan office on the highway in Clayburn in 2009 and keeps a lot of repossessed trucks behind it. Leon Varner has done his collecting in the south end of the county for six years.

npcs.name: Garland Teasley
npcs.where: Calder, in a private office above a bank on the courthouse square
npcs.reach: by letter; he does not take calls from people who owe him
npcs.role: a private lender in Calder who carries the Sturdivant timber loans
npcs.look: Frail, immaculate man of seventy-four in a three-piece suit and a hearing aid, with a cane, a pocket watch and a hand that shakes until he signs something.
npcs.voice: Soft and precise; speaks of debts as obligations and people as accounts, and has never in his life raised his voice.
npcs.goal: Get his money out of Sturdivant Land and Timber before the bridge vote decides what the land is worth.
npcs.secret: He means to call in the timber loans the week after the vote, whichever way it goes, and he has been selling off his small notes to raise cash first.
npcs.history: Garland Teasley has lent money privately out of the same office in Calder since 1975. He lent to Harlan Voss for thirty years, and now Carter Sturdivant drives up to see him every quarter.

npcs.name: Teresa Gaines
npcs.where: a parole office two states over
npcs.reach: her office line; she returns calls within the week
npcs.role: a parole officer two states over
npcs.look: Square, short-haired woman of forty-four in a polo shirt with a state seal, with a lanyard, a coffee thermos and a caseload of ninety.
npcs.voice: Flat and fast; reads out conditions in the same tone as the weather and says I have ninety of you.
npcs.goal: Find the parolees who stopped reporting before their warrants become somebody else's problem.
npcs.secret: Boyd Teague is on her caseload, he missed his check-in last week, and the violation she filed means one call from anyone in Lockett's Ferry would bring a warrant.
npcs.history: Teresa Gaines has supervised parolees for fifteen years out of a county office two states over. Nobody in Lockett's Ferry has heard of her.

factions.name: Sturdivant Land and Timber
factions.goal: Get the old bridge closed and the new state bridge built five miles downstream on Sturdivant bottomland, then sell the state the right-of-way and put a truck stop at the new interchange.
factions.methods: Private loans and contracts for deed that can be called in on a week's notice, a mayor paid in cash, a bridge report bought from the engineer the state sent, and Neal Haverty, a lawyer in Calder.

onComplete.text: Carter Sturdivant tears up the note on Pittman's Gas and Service in front of Royce Pittman, and Royce promises him his vote for the downstream site at Tuesday's council meeting.

rumour.text: Carter Sturdivant tore up the note on Royce Pittman's station, and Royce has promised him his vote on the bridge.

The mayor meets Carter Sturdivant in the motel parking lot once a month after dark, and she never goes inside.
Travis Cagle bought a new bass boat this summer and pays the note down in cash every month, and nobody pays for a boat like that on a night-shift salary.
The pills at Riverbend come from Colt Purvis, and his uncle Wade either does not know or does not want to.
Royce Pittman owes the Sturdivants on the station, which is why he still will not say how he will vote.
Miss Vada will not sign the bottomland over for the new bridge, and Carter cannot sell it without her.
The mayor wants to get rid of the police and hand the town to the county sheriff before Christmas.
Something in the deep hole under the old bridge pulls a swimmer down every seven years, and this is the seventh year.
Loretta Gaddis has already sold the Low Water to the Sturdivants and is only waiting for the bridge to close to tell anyone.
June Satterfield lost her nursing license for stealing pills from the hospital, and that is where the Riverbend pills come from.
Mavis Mangum rings up a cash room at the motor court now and then that never makes it into the book.
Carter Sturdivant has been after Odessa Fairley to tell Dr. Sayle in Calder that his mother is losing her mind.
Nikki Ballard drove up to the sheriff's office in Clayburn on her day off, and it was not to pay a ticket.
Lamar Haskins has a check from Carter Sturdivant in his glove box that he has never cashed.
Micah Dees is down at the landing past midnight most nights, and the pastor thinks he is asleep in his bed.
Darlene Pittman keeps a folder in the station safe that Royce is not allowed to open.
Curtis Pruett holds every deck up to the lamp before he deals his Friday game, and he says the next marked deck he finds goes in the river.
Wade Purvis buys cartons for cash at the landing, a dollar a pack over what Pittman's charges, and asks no questions.
Dwight Spann was out on the bottomland with a flashlight and a can of survey paint the night before the state crew came to look at it.
For forty dollars, Nadine Dees will write a baptism into the church book any way you need it, and the county takes a church record as proof of birth.
